title: idle_status -- what the console shows when nothing runs (plan.md 15.1 item 3)
description: Outside a run the runtime holds nothing open, so idle status is a FILE THE RUNTIME WRITES, never a device the console asks. It lives at microscope_runtime/.runtime_status/idle_status.json, which the validator's walk skips and .gitignore hides, because it is VOLATILE AND NEVER A RECORD: it is rewritten at the end of every run, a check-now run included, and everything it says is already in that run's own log, which is the record. Written atomically (a temporary file renamed over it), so a reader never sees half of one. Every value carries the time it was read, and NOTHING IS CARRIED FORWARD: a channel the last run did not open is absent or shown as not opened, never given an older value. The registry's fixed facts are POINTED TO, by path and sha256, and not copied, because knowledge lives in one place (P14). The view says "as of written_at, from written_by_run"; an absent file is "no status yet", which is not "nothing connected" (manager-console-office-20261017-1, 2026-10-22).

last_run.description: the most recent run of any kind, a check-now run included; null before the first

kind.description: lights_off: the host's run of its own kind for a lights-off request outside a run (run_interface.schema.json lights_off_request); a lights-off during a run is that run's stop and leaves the run's own kind

outcome.description: run_ended's reason, as the log has it

preflight.description: the last preflight's rows as the log has them, with when; null when the run reached no preflight

last_snapshot.description: the last snapshot of the run, one reading per channel the run opened; null when it took none

check_now.description: the last check-now run; null before the first

closed.description: null when it was never opened

error.description: what the open, read or close raised, as the runtime caught it. Present when a step failed; a channel that was simply not opened carries none. It says why the channel went unread, never what its state was

ownership.description: per resource, which maker program holds which interface (4.6.10). Until that check exists this says not_built, and the console shows no verdict rather than a guess

registry.description: the device registry this runtime read, by path and the sha256 of its bytes

light_path_order.description: optional until the runtime writes it (card 104); then written by every run

reading.description: one channel as a run read it. A value is shown only beside the time it was read and how; a channel with no time is unknown, never current

name.description: the channel's display name, as the registry the run read gave it, so a reader needs no store to name it

how.description: read_back: the device answered a read. not_readable: the registry says this channel has no read-back, so what is shown is what was sent. not_read: the run did not reach it, or it was busy, and the value is null

t_wall.description: when this value was read; null exactly when how is not_read

value.description: what was read, or for not_readable what was last sent in this run; null when not_read

light_path_order.description: the order of the stand's elements along each branch of the light path (plan.md 15.1 item 11), as the runtime read it from its envelope snapshot, written beside the elements here and as `light_path_order` in every `snapshot` event of events.jsonl in this same shape. The page reads it from those two places only. It commands nothing. not_in_snapshot: the snapshot holds no order, so the page draws no order and says why. read: the order, with the grade and the source the store gives it, as the store spells them; the page says the grade in words and, for a source that is a description, "from a description, not checked on this microscope". Both carry hand_set, the elements moved by hand with their slots by the registry's names, which comes from the registry and not from the order

channel.description: the registry channel the element is reached through; null for an element with none (the polarizer, the eyepieces), which the page draws as "no channel"

items.description: one position of an element moved by hand. name is the slot's word as the registry the run read gives it, null when the registry gives none. resolves is true only when the registry gives the slot a name and an entry for it, so a required-state selector naming it can be checked; otherwise false, with why, and the page shows the slot as one a plan cannot name and refuses it by that name

read_back.description: where this element's read-back row is in a snapshot: the channel whose snapshot carries it and the key it carries it under, exactly as the snapshot spells it (a registry id such as nosepiece, or a Micro-Manager label such as DiaLamp). Written by the runtime from the registry and the backend it read, never derived by the page. The page joins an element to a row on this pair and nothing else; null means the element has no read-back row, and the page shows it as not read back rather than matching on the element id

hand_set.description: the elements moved by hand, each with its slots by the registry's names; read from the registry the run read and not from the order, so it is written whether or not the snapshot holds an order

entry_ref.description: the store entry that holds the order

source.description: the entry's source, as the store holds it

source_kind.description: the part of source before its first colon, as the store spells it; the page maps a kind to its words and shows a kind it does not know as unknown, never as observed

items.description: one branch of the light path. elements is in the order light meets them, as the order in the snapshot gives it, and the array's order is the only position there is. place_not_recorded lists the elements the order names for this branch without a place; they carry no position and the page never draws them into one
